sections.content: How many people are "refuse and salvage occupations"?

38,045 people

were counted on the census as "refuse and salvage occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Refuse and salvage collectors supervise and carry out the collection and processing of refuse from household, commercial and industrial premises.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "refuse and salvage occupations" there were more men than women (93.2% compared with 6.8%).

This means "refuse and salvage occupations" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 93.2% and women made up 6.8% of "refuse and salvage occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "refuse and salvage occupations" included:

  • mechanical engineers
  • painters and decorators
  • computer system and equipment installers and servicers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "refuse and salvage occupations" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "refuse and salvage occupations", 13.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "refuse and salvage occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

  • paper and wood machine operatives
  • assemblers and routine operatives (other)
  • plant and machine operatives (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "refuse and salvage occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "refuse and salvage occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "refuse and salvage occupations", 10.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (88.9% compared with 11.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.7%) than self-employed (6.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
